Package neqsim.process.equipment.capacity

Class EquipmentLimitRegister

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.capacity.EquipmentLimitRegister
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class EquipmentLimitRegister extends Object implements Serializable
Register of equipment limits that carry their source and status: one entry per equipment tag, quantity and validity period, with a value, a unit, the document or rule the number comes from, a EquipmentLimitRegister.Status (VERIFIED or ASSUMPTION) and a confidence.

The register holds plant equipment limits (per tag, quantity and validity period) with provenance. The file format is a documented JSON layout: 

 {
   "meta": {"title": "...", "built": "..."},
   "limits": [
     {"equipmentTag": "K-201", "quantity": "n_max", "value": 10278.0, "unit": "rpm",
      "validFromYear": null, "validToYear": 2028, "source": "SPD As-Used 2025-07-08",
      "status": "VERIFIED", "confidence": "medium", "authority": "VENDOR_DATASHEET", "note": ""}
   ]
 }

Only equipmentTag, quantity and value are required. status defaults to ASSUMPTION; confidence is a fraction in [0, 1] or one of high (0.9), medium (0.6) and low (0.3); validFromYear/validToYear are inclusive and may be null (open). authority is the name of a CapacityConstraint.ConstraintSource (default USER_RULE).

fromCompressorLimitsDatabase(String) reads a nested machines/facts compressor-limits layout into the same entries, so a database snapshot can be loaded, queried and merged into a process model. applyTo(ProcessSystem, Integer) writes the limits into the capacity constraints of the equipment whose name equals the tag as operating limits with the status and source in the source reference, so they appear in the utilisation snapshot with their provenance. A quantity is applied only to a constraint of matching unit; the rest is listed in the EquipmentLimitRegister.ApplyReport instead of being silently dropped.

    • applyTo

      public EquipmentLimitRegister.ApplyReport applyTo(ProcessSystem process, Integer year)
      Write the limits into the capacity constraints of a process model. Every equipment whose name equals an entry tag (compared after normalizeTag(String)) and that has the mapped constraint receives the value as operating limit, with the status and source in the source reference and the confidence attached. The default mapping is n_max to speed, n_min to minSpeed and T_out_max to dischargeTemperature; add more with mapQuantityToConstraint(String, String). A quantity without a mapping, a missing constraint or a unit that cannot be converted is reported in EquipmentLimitRegister.ApplyReport.getSkipped().
      Parameters:
      process - process system whose unit names are matched against the tags
      year - year for the validity selection, or null for any
      Returns:
      report of the applied and skipped limits

    • fromCompressorLimitsDatabase

      public static EquipmentLimitRegister fromCompressorLimitsDatabase(String json)
      Read a register from the nested compressor-limits layout (machines with a facts object per machine; each fact has value, unit, source, status and note). The record-level era_from/era_to become the validity period and the record confidence the entry confidence; facts without a numeric value are skipped. The fact names are kept as quantity keys (power_limit, n_max, p_out_max, T_out_max, ...). The tag is the record tag (the machine key if absent), so the hardware eras of one machine (keys K-201 and K-201_N) share the tag and are told apart by the year in lookup(String, String, Integer).
      Parameters:
      json - text of the database file
      Returns:
      the register
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the JSON has no machines object
